# RUSTSEC-2026-0369

Four zip < 9.0.0 extraction advisories (SUID/SGID
bits preserved; symlink targets outside the destination; permissions
applied through symlinks; and, 0429, dated 2026-10-22 and first seen
red-ing `security` on main 2026-11-02, the process ABORTS on a
symlink entry with a large declared size). All four live in
`ZipArchive::extract()` and `ZipStreamReader::extract()`. The
runner's OWN zip dependency is bumped to 9 (patched), and runner code
never calls `extract()`.

The ignore covers the SECOND copy, zip 4.6.1, which enters only as

    qontinui-runner -> tauri-plugin-updater -> zip ^4

and every tauri-plugin-updater through 2.14.0 requires `zip ^4`.
2.14.1, the first on `zip ^9`, requires tauri ^2.12, so it is not
reachable from here without a tauri upgrade. Not exploitable in that
path. The updater calls `extract()` only from its Windows
`extract_zip`. 0367 and 0369 need Unix permission bits, which zip 4
never applies on Windows. 0368 and 0429
are NOT ruled out by the platform: zip 4 creates symlinks on Windows
too, and 0429's abort is a denial of service on any OS.
What rules out all four is that `extract_zip` runs only AFTER
`verify_signature` checks the downloaded bundle against our updater
public key, so the archive is not attacker-controlled. For 0429 that
means triggering the abort needs the updater signing key, and whoever
holds that key can already ship arbitrary code. The runner reaches
the updater only through `download_and_install`
(commands/execution/system_ops.rs), and the frontend is granted no
`updater:` permission.

This ignore can go once the runner is on tauri-plugin-updater >= 2.14.1,
the first release on zip ^9 (published 2026-10-28). That release
requires tauri ^2.12, and this lock is on tauri 2.11.1, so taking it
is a tauri upgrade (watch the vendored tao-0.35.0 patch). Tracking:
qontinui/qontinui-runner#2500. REVIEW BY 2026-12-02. Re-assess
immediately if updater signature checking is ever disabled or
bypassed, if runner code starts calling `extract()` on a zip 4
archive, or if the updater extracts on Unix.

This rationale is shared with RUSTSEC-2026-0367, RUSTSEC-2026-0368, RUSTSEC-2026-0429, which were ignored together (one comment block in ci.yml before the move to one file per advisory).

Drop when the runner is on tauri-plugin-updater >= 2.14.1 (the first release on zip ^9), so no zip < 9.0.0 is left in Cargo.lock.
